reason: E3 directly supports the core premise that phase-selective recrystallization of the soft phase in a eutectic HEA dramatically improves ductility and strength, and E1 confirms that semi-coherent boundaries and dislocation pile-ups are key to the brittleness mechanism. However, the specific annealing temperature (~700 °C) and the claim of 10–20 percentage point ductility increase are not explicitly supported by the cited passages, and E2 mainly describes the problem rather than the solution.
premises: Dislocation pile-ups at semi-coherent phase boundaries in eutectic HEAs cause local stress concentrations and microcracking, limiting ductility.
Phase-selective recrystallization of the ductile FCC phase can eliminate weak boundaries and release strain hardening capacity in duplex alloys.
Annealing at ~700 °C can trigger recrystallization in the FCC phase of eutectic HEAs without altering the hard phase network.
A recrystallized soft phase embedded in a hard skeleton improves strain partitioning and homogeneous deformation, enhancing ductility.
The treated alloy can achieve high uniform elongation (~35%) and high true stress (~2 GPa), matching or exceeding as-cast strength.
